results.fact: Pitch count: `pitches` (5) vs pitch_detail's numbered rows (only 4 accounted for)
results.correct_value: 5 pitches: P1 4th class, P2 low 5th to a notch below a gendarme, P3 5.6 crux around the gendarme, P4 low 5th to the cockscomb, P5 low 5th to the summit
results.evidence: pitches=5, the itinerary ('the 5 pitches'), detailed_rack (5.6 crux on pitch 3, belay at the P2/P3 notch below the gendarme) and pro_needs (pitch 3 crux, belayers on pitch 2) all describe a five-pitch route with the crux on P3. The only published description of this 2014 route gives exactly five pitches: 4th, low 5th, 5.6 crux bypassing the gendarme on the right, low 5th, low 5th. pitch_detail rewritten into five rows in original wording; its old 'good quality rock' note also contradicted the loose/lichen-covered rock stated elsewhere on the row.

results.fact: Descent method: rappels/itinerary say descend via the North Ridge (1 rappel), but descent/descent_text/bail describe reversing the South Ridge itself
results.evidence: The only published description of this route says to descend via the North Ridge (whose descent is a single ~40-ft rappel then reversing that ridge, per a guide-service profile of the North Ridge). Within the row, rappels and itinerary say North Ridge while descent and descent_text say reverse the South Ridge (bail concerns mid-route retreat). Only one source addresses the South Ridge descent and the row is split 2-2, so no patch under the two-source rule; likely answer is descend the North Ridge.

results.evidence: pro_needs and detailed_rack both put the crux on pitch 3 around the gendarme, and the published pitch-by-pitch description puts the 5.6 crux on pitch 3. Resolved by the same pitch_detail set patch listed under the pitch-count contradiction (not repeated here to avoid a double compare-and-set).

results.fact: gain_ft (1,900 ft) is implausibly low for this route's own trailhead-to-summit elevation difference (~4,000 ft)
results.evidence: The Boston Basin trailhead is at 3,200 ft (two guide services, matching the row's trailhead waypoint) and the Aiguille de l'M is 7,200 ft (route database area elevation, matching high_point_ft and the Summit waypoint). Minimum car-to-summit gain is therefore 4,000 ft, exactly the sibling North Ridge's gain_ft for the same trailhead and summit; 1,900 ft is impossible. No loss_ft or itinerary gain numbers exist on the row to reconcile.
